South Africa Cricket Test Match Affected by Rain, Trade Relations with US Sour

The second cricket Test match between South Africa and Australia at St. George's Park in Gqeberha was significantly impacted by rain, with Day 1 seeing only a partial session of play and South Africa ending at 20-2. Later in the match, on Day 3, Temba Bavuma scored 179 runs, helping South Africa turn the tables on Australia. Australian bowler Boland took wickets, contributing to South Africa's struggles at various points, with the team reaching 97-5 at one stage. Separately, South African President Ramaphosa is preparing the nation for a potential trade disruption with the US due to an executive action by Trump, which threatens thousands of jobs. This situation is leading South Africa to explore increased trade with China and India as its ties with the US reportedly sour.
